title: Understanding Quantum Instruments
summary: The quantum instrument (QI) formalism is required to model mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) and the dependence of the post-measurement state on the measurement outcome. Correctly modeling QIs is essential for applications using MCMs, such as adaptive circuits and quantum error correction. Although QIs yield a joint quantum-classical state after measurement, errors in QIs can still be represented by a $d^2 \times d^2$ superoperator (e.g., process or transfer matrix) for each outcome, just as superoperators describe Markovian errors on unitary gates.
